approachQuestion.prompt:
Count compatible position pairs

Input: an array weights and an integer target. Return the number of index pairs (i,j) with i<j and weights[i]+weights[j]=target. Distinct positions count separately even if values match.

Example 1: weights = [2,2,5,5], target = 7. Output: 4. Example 2: weights = [3,3,3], target = 6. Output: 3. Example 3: weights = [1], target = 2. Output: 0. 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000; target is a signed 32-bit integer. The answer fits signed 64-bit arithmetic.

Constraints: input is immutable; all identifiers and numeric entries are signed 32-bit integers unless specified. Arithmetic uses signed 64-bit integers. Prefer the least expected running-time growth, then avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Non-adversarial hashing of fixed-size integer keys/tuples has expected amortized constant cost.

options.text: Scan left to right with a frequency map of earlier values. Add the stored frequency of target−current to the answer, then increment current’s frequency.
options.feedback: Each pair is counted at its later index, and a frequency contributes one pair per eligible earlier position. Querying first excludes self-pairs.

options.text: Sort a copied array, move inward with two pointers, and multiply run sizes for unequal matched values; for equal matched values add k(k−1)/2 for the remaining run.
options.feedback: Run multiplicities make this correct, but comparison sorting is removable when prior frequencies can be looked up directly.

options.text: Use a set of earlier values and add one whenever the complement is present.
options.feedback: [2,2,5] with target 7 has two pairs, but membership alone contributes only one when 5 arrives.

options.text: Increment the current frequency before looking up its complement, adding that frequency to the answer.
options.feedback: [3] with target 6 contributes one invalid self-pair. The map must contain only earlier positions.

feedback.reason: Use prior multiplicity, rather than membership alone, to count every pair exactly once.
details: Scan the input with an initially empty prior-frequency map and a 64-bit answer. Add the complement’s prior count, then increment the current value’s count.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Count compatible position pairs — analyzed method”, n is the array length and u is its number of distinct values. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input of size n, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

O(u+1) for prior frequencies, counters and constant call stack. The scalar output is excluded.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(u + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.
“Expected O(n² + 1) time; O(u + 1) space.”: Pair contributions are added as counts, not enumerated one pair at a time.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(1) space.”: The prior-frequency map can contain u keys.
“Guaranteed O(n + 1) time for every hash distribution; O(u + 1) space.”: The hashing model guarantees expected amortized costs only.
